title: Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.10 — Personal actions
content:
Ohio Rev. Code § 2305.10

(A) Except as provided in division (C) or (D) of this section or in section 2305.19 of the Revised Code, an action for any of the following shall be brought within two years after the cause of action accrued:

(1) An action for bodily injury or injury to personal property;

(2) An action for libel, slander, assault, battery, or false imprisonment.

title: Ohio Rev. Code § 1302.72 — Statute of limitations in contracts for sale
content:
Ohio Rev. Code § 1302.72

(A) An action for breach of any contract for sale must be commenced within four years after the cause of action has accrued. By the original agreement the parties may reduce the period of limitation to not less than one year but may not extend it.

title: Sheeley v. Memorial Hospital, 66 Ohio St. 3d 325 (1993)
content:
Sheeley v. Memorial Hospital, 66 Ohio St. 3d 325 (1993).

[Excerpt — holding summary.]

The Supreme Court of Ohio held that a hospital may be liable for medical malpractice when it fails to ensure that physicians with staff privileges meet minimum competency standards.

opinionParts.content: A hospital may be liable when it fails to ensure that physicians with staff privileges meet minimum competency standards.
